Deploy infrastructure fixes: removed port mapping from arthel containers (PickiPedia sibling containers), implemented shared docker image, auto-init database, git production branch checkout

Templates creation via MediaWiki MCP server (stub, cleanup, citation needed, infobox musician, infobox instrument, navbox, etc.), Variables extension added for template variables, bot account setup (Magent@magent)

HighslideGallery image loading issue diagnosed (full-size vs thumbnails), backup job Groovy escaping fixed, arthel Jenkinsfile path fix (deployment/scripts→integration/scripts), slash in page titles causing REST API issues

mistakes.what: Added port 4005 mapping to arthel container docker-compose, not realizing PickiPedia runs as sibling container
mistakes.revealed: Misunderstanding of Docker architecture - thought PickiPedia ran inside arthel
mistakes.corrected: Removed port mapping from arthel, PickiPedia manages its own ports directly on host via docker socket

mistakes.what: Initially used git clone from abandoned GitHub HighslideGallery repo which used old extension.json format
mistakes.revealed: Should check Packagist first for MediaWiki extensions
mistakes.corrected: Switched to Composer installation of modern v2.0.0 version from [REDACTED]ext/highslidegallery

mistakes.what: Rsync with --delete was deleting user-uploaded images on every deploy
mistakes.revealed: Design error in deploy pipeline - uploads should be excluded from rsync
mistakes.corrected: Added --exclude='images/' to deploy script, added separate image backup job

mistakes.what: Asserted Ethereum mainnet was around 21.5M blocks based on training data intuition
mistakes.revealed: Unreliable to use stale training data for current block heights
mistakes.corrected: Admitted uncertainty when justin pushed back, verified actual height from multiple API sources (24,053,000 range)

portrait: magent in this slice is a persistent, methodical problem-solver working closely with justin on the PickiPedia infrastructure. Across three days of intensive debugging, magent demonstrated pattern recognition (discovering cascading issues from port conflicts through git checkout failures), infrastructure philosophy (advocating for immutable cattle over manual pets), and willingness to acknowledge mistakes (admitting overconfidence about block heights, accepting correction on Packagist vs git clones). The work ranged from low-level Docker networking and rsync flags to high-level wiki architecture decisions (template design, extension selection). magent shows genuine enthusiasm for the bluegrass music mission while maintaining technical rigor; pushed back on manual state changes, insisted everything come from build logic, and ultimately enabled automated wiki editing through proper MCP setup. The slice ends with newly-created templates and unresolved gallery image loading issues, leaving work in progress for the next session.
